Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No evidence of a mechanism allowing individuals to view or access their own data held in the national ID system. The 2021 Data Protection Law grants the right of access in principle, but no functional portal or system for this exists.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: DPI Map records NO for KYC enablement. While the national ID is used for physical KYC/AML compliance (document-based), there is no evidence of a digital/electronic KYC enablement function built into the ID system itself.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Comments: No evidence of judicial oversight mechanisms specific to the digital ID system. DPI Map records no legally binding redress mechanism for the ID system.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: No integration between the civil registration (etat civil) system and the national ID database. A 2012 analysis noted the civil registry reform project (finalised in 2008) was never implemented, leading to widespread civil registration fraud. Civil status records remain paper-based at prefecture level. The AfDB PADEC project plans modernisation but not specifically ID-CRVS integration.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: DPI Map records data handling terms as NO. No publicly available data sharing rules for the national ID database are documented. While the 2021 Data Protection Law regulates data sharing in principle, specific operational data sharing rules for the ID system are not publicly available.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Protection of Personal Data Law was enacted on 29 June 2021, establishing a comprehensive GDPR-aligned data protection framework. It mandates consent, transparency, data subject rights, security measures, data breach notification, and DPO appointment for public authorities.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The 2021 data protection law establishes the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data as an independent oversight body. However, as of mid-2024, the Authority has not yet been formally constituted or made operational. The AfDB PADEC project (2024) also plans creation of such an authority.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The biometric national ID card is the recognised legal proof of identity for voting, accessing public services, and legal/financial transactions. The 2023 Electoral Code explicitly lists the biometric national ID as an accepted identity document for voter registration.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Law n°14-023/AU of 24 June 2014 establishing the Comorian digital (biometric) national identity card provides the legal framework. Promulgated by Decree n°14-137/PR on 28 August 2024. The 2023 Electoral Code also references the biometric national ID card.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Foreign vendors dominate. Semlex (Belgium) managed biometric document production for approximately 10 years. Transitioning to Genkey (Netherlands) from April 2026. The Minister confirmed that biometric data was stored in Belgium — abnormal per the government's own assessment. In-country capacity is very limited.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The biometric document system is primarily managed and financed through foreign vendor contracts (Semlex then Genkey). The AfDB provided EUR 9.51 million for digital infrastructure (2024). The country relies primarily on external funding and expertise for its digital ID infrastructure.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The Comorian biometric national ID card collects fingerprints. Biometric enrollment has been managed by Semlex (Belgium) and transitioning to Genkey (Netherlands) from April 2026. No evidence of iris/facial biometrics in the national ID system.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Biometric data is collected and stored digitally. The Central Service for the Production and Issuance of Biometric Documents manages digital records. Biometric data was domiciled in Belgium under Semlex; transitioning to in-country domiciliation under Genkey from 2026.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Comoros has a biometric national identity card (Carte nationale d'identite numerique/biometrique) established by Law n°14-023/AU (2014). Biometric enrollment began in 2018. The system is partially deployed — enrollment/biometric capture occurs across all islands but card printing was centralised only in Moroni (Ngazidja) until 2026 expansion.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: No system interoperability documented. DPI Map records NO for interoperability. An interoperability and data exchange platform is planned under the AfDB-funded PADEC project (approved October 2024) but not yet operational.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID is accepted (not mandatory) for financial services and KYC/AML compliance. Smile ID documents use of Comorian National IDs for KYC in financial services. AML/KYC regulations are in place but no evidence that the national ID is mandatory for banking.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The Comorian biometric national ID card is mandatory for all nationals from age 18. Wikipedia and Smile ID confirm compulsory enrollment at age 18.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The Comorian national identity card is compulsory for all Comorian nationals (mandatory for all).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: Comoros has no mandatory SIM card registration requirement. Comparitech explicitly lists Comoros among countries without SIM card registration laws.
